initial_plan.denominator: number of police-reported crash rows in that calendar year
initial_plan.population: police-reported NYC crash rows with crash_date in calendar years 2013 through 2025 inclusive; numerator counts motorist deaths attributed to those crashes, including zero-death crashes in the denominator

final_plan.can_answer: partly: motorist deaths per police-reported crash describe a crash-record outcome frequency, but without miles driven this data cannot say whether risk per mile declined
final_plan.metric: annual number_of_motorist_killed divided by annual police-reported crash rows, expressed as recorded motorist deaths per 100,000 crashes
final_plan.denominator: all police-reported crash rows in that calendar year, including rows with zero motorist deaths
final_plan.population: police-reported NYC crash rows dated in calendar years 2013 through 2025 inclusive; motorist deaths are summed over those crashes
final_plan.years: 2013–2025 inclusive, each observed from January 1 through December 31
final_plan.limitations: The file has no miles-driven or other travel-exposure denominator and cannot measure risk per mile. The ratio is deaths per crash-record, not a person's probability of death or risk while driving. Annual crash-row denominators differ: they changed by 98,568 rows from 2019 to 2020 (211,486 to 112,918), so changes in this ratio across those years can arise from the denominator change and are compared with that caution. The check found 0 NULL crash dates and 0 missing motorist-death counts in plan years; every selected year has full-year date coverage, so no plan-year rows are dropped for these missing fields.
